activate_user.description: Activate a staged or deactivated user. With the email off, Okta returns the activation link instead of sending it.
activate_user.name: activate_user

parameters.description: The Okta user id (00u...), the user's login, or the Admin Console URL of their profile.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: Turn on to have Okta email the user. Off returns the activation link to this workflow instead.
parameters.name: send_email

activation_token.description: The one-time token behind that link, for building your own activation URL.

activation_url.description: The link the user follows to finish activating, returned only when the email was not sent.

asynchronous.description: True when Okta completes this operation in the background, so the user's own status may still say otherwise for a moment.

status.description: The status this operation moves the user to. Read the user again if you need to confirm the transition has landed.

add_user_to_group.description: Add a user to an Okta group. Safe to re-run, because Okta accepts it whether or not they were already a member.

parameters.name: group_id

group_id.description: The group they were added to.

member.description: True once the user is in the group.

create_group.description: Create an Okta group. Groups made this way are Okta groups, the only kind whose membership an API can change.

profile.name: Support Engineers

parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What the group is for.
parameters.name: description

group.description: The group Okta created. Use 'id' to add members to it.

create_user.description: Create a user in your Okta org. Left unactivated they are staged and cannot sign in; activated without a password Okta emails them an activation link.
create_user.name: create_user

parameters.description: The user's primary email address.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: The user's given name.
parameters.name: first_name

parameters.description: The user's family name.
parameters.name: last_name

parameters.description: The username they sign in with. Defaults to the email address, which is what most orgs require.
parameters.name: login

parameters.description: An initial password, validated against your org's password policy. Leave blank to have Okta send an activation link instead.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: The user's mobile number.
parameters.name: mobile_phone

parameters.description: The user's job title.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: The department the user belongs to.
parameters.name: department

parameters.description: Group ids to add the user to as they are created, up to 20.
parameters.name: group_ids

parameters.description: Turn on to activate the user immediately. Off leaves them staged, and nothing is emailed.
parameters.name: activate

user.description: The user Okta created. Use 'id' for every later step: a login can change, an id cannot.

delete_group.description: Delete an Okta group. Its members keep their accounts; only the group and its assignments go.
delete_group.name: delete_group

parameters.name: group_id

deleted.description: Always true; a failure raises instead.

delete_user.description: Permanently delete a user. Okta only deletes a deactivated user, so an active one is deactivated first, which cannot be recovered.
delete_user.name: delete_user

parameters.description: The Okta user id (00u...), the user's login, or the Admin Console URL of their profile.
parameters.name: user_id

deactivated_first.description: True when the user still had to be deactivated, which takes a second delete call.

deleted.description: Always true; a failure raises instead.

previous_status.description: The status the user held before deletion.
